newsitem.title: USA: Gore, Chernomyrdin draw boos from furious auto show fans.
newsitem.headline: Gore, Chernomyrdin draw boos from furious auto show fans.

text.p: Hundreds of people at Chicago's annual auto show, irked at being kept behind velvet ropes, booed throughout an appearance by U.S. Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

Despite apologies from Gore and Chicago Mayor Richard Daley for keeping the public out while Chernomyrdin and Russian officials viewed the show privately, the crowd kept up catcalls during brief remarks by the Chernomyrdin.

"I want to say hello to everybody," he said through an interpreter at the opening of the week-long auto exhibition, shouting through the boos. "You make great cars. Let's get into these cars and go into the future."
The Russian dignitaries, along with Gore and his wife Tipper, got a private tour of the show, held in the cavernous McCormick Place Exhibition Centre in Chicago's downtown Loop district.
As a result, members of the public were kept out of the exhibition area 45 minutes past the 10 a.m. CST (1500 GMT) opening time.

Inside the hall, Chernomyrdin and Gore walked the lanes of U.S. cars, and got onto a raised platform to sit in a sporty purple two-seater, a Plymouth Prowler. Chernomyrdin was behind the wheel and Gore rode shotgun.

They also stopped in front of a so-called "concept" car, a gold Chrysler Phaeton, which was attended by a promoter for the cars, 25-year-old Shannon Clark, who wore a black suit with tiny sparkles, ultra-high heels and a riding hat with veil.

The nasty brush with the public at the exhibition hall was a far cry from the decorous meetings Chernomyrdin and Gore held on Thursday and Friday in Washington, where the biggest conflict was over Russia's fears about NATO expansion.
The two Numbers Twos made a flying trip to the Midwest to mingle with U.S. heartland business leaders to drum up support for foreign investment in Russia.
This is the eighth time Gore and Chernomyrdin have met in this forum in the last four years. Their eponymous commission was originally aimed at dismantling barriers to technological cooperation.

However, as Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health has worsened -- he is recovering from quintuple heart bypass surgery in November and pneumonia in January -- Chernomyrdin and Gore have become the key diplomatic channel between the two countries.
On Friday, the two announced a summit between Yeltsin and President Bill Clinton on March 20-21 in Helsinki, Finland, a location chosen for its proximity to Yeltsin's Moscow home base.
